messages:
maria: FYI customer TW-431 says their invoice is ~22% higher than the SDK's token estimator. Invoice INV-9042. They run a streaming chat flow that triggers tool calls.

devin: Can you paste a minimal repro (curl + SDK snippet) and the model/SDK versions?

maria: Model: redwood-chat-xl-qa, SDK-js 0.9.2. Repro below (redacted keys):

```
# curl repro
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "redwood-chat-xl-qa",
    "messages": [{"role":"system","content":"You are an assistant."}, {"role":"user","content":"Search for climate policy docs and summarize"}],
    "stream": false
  }'
```

API response snippet (server shows usage):

```
{"id":"c-123","choices":[...],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":180,"completion_tokens":144,"total_tokens":324}}
```

SDK estimator output from customer (approx):

```
// sdk estimator
const est = estimator.countTokens(messages)
console.log('est', est) // 252
```

sre-bot: linked invoice INV-9042 to this thread :link: 

devin: I repro'd locally with the same prompt. Observed server usage.total_tokens=328 vs SDK estimator ~252. Quick hypothesis: runtime appends tool/function call payloads or debug traces after the SDK runs its local estimator, and those server-side additions are included in billing.

ingrid: Billing note — we charge based on the runtime's usage.total_tokens. If the runtime attaches tool output or internal diagnostics into the completion stream, those tokens count unless the runtime explicitly strips them for billing. We don't retroactively change invoices without evidence.

maria: Customer insists they never enabled debug. They do call our search tool via function-calls; sometimes the tool returns long raw snippets (search hits). They expected the estimator to match the invoice.

devin: I inspected the raw JSON coming back from the runtime: the top-level choice includes an extra field used for orchestration:

```
"tool_trace": {
  "search_results": "<long blob of snippets>"
}
```

That tool_trace content is concatenated into the streamed completion by the runtime for convenience in older deploys; the local SDK estimator doesn't see that because it only tokenizes the messages array before the runtime mutates the final output.

devin: Root cause = mismatch in where tokenization runs: SDK estimates pre-runtime messages; runtime may append tool payloads and internal notes that are billed. Fix options:
- Make SDK prefer server-reported usage (response.usage.total_tokens) when present (recommended for exact billing).
- Add a server flag to exclude debug/tool_trace from billing and keep them out of the final completion used for tokenization.
- Update SDK estimator to simulate post-runtime appenders (hard/imprecise).

ingrid: For INV-9042 we can offer a one-time credit contingent on the customer confirming they did not intentionally include large search results. Send me the curl + response JSON and the customer's SDK logs.

maria: Sent curl and full response JSON to ingrid (via secure share). Customer accepted a credit for this invoice for now.

devin: Short-term workaround for customers: use the server-provided usage field instead of client-side estimator. Example:

```
const resp = await client.chat.create(...)
console.log('billed_tokens', resp.usage.total_tokens)
```

Longer-term: I'll open a PR to have the SDK surface a warning when estimator vs server usage diverge >5% and to document this behaviour. PR opened: #3425, ETA EOD tomorrow.

carmen: +1 on the warning — saved us in past disputes.

maria: Thanks all :thumbsup: I'll follow up with the customer once we have the PR and billing credit confirmation.

devin: I'll also add a short KB entry in Support docs explaining tool calls can add server-side tokens and how to use resp.usage to reconcile.

maria: closing loop once KB + PR are live.
